deviations.what: The anti-join that removes base classes joins only on (year, cls) and omits firm_id, so a class in any firm's base set for year t is dropped from every other firm's forward set, which breaks rule 7 (B(i,t) is firm-specific) and rule 10 (firm separation).

notes: Everything else matches: filing_year dating, the cpc_seq == 0 filter, missing-class exclusion, base years t+1 to t+5 and forward years t-1 to t-3 with t excluded, the NA and 0 rules, collapsing of duplicate firm_year rows, and the output columns. Focal years 1987-2015 are not enforced in build.R; it uses whatever years the caller passes in firm_year, which I did not count as a deviation.
